record.original_question: For each dimension d, what is the greatest possible volume of a pair of spherical orbifolds of dimension d that are Laplace-isospectral but not isometric?

evidence.quote: Question 1.4. What is the largest volume of an isospectral pair of d-dimensional non-isometric spherical orbifolds?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A spherical orbifold of dimension d is a quotient S^d/Γ, where S^d denotes the unit round sphere in R^{d+1} and Γ is a finite subgroup of the orthogonal group O(d+1) acting on S^d. Two such orbifolds are said to be Laplace-isospectral if the Laplace–Beltrami operators on their smooth parts have the same spectrum (with multiplicities), and they are isometric if there is a volume- and metric-preserving bijection between them; equivalently, S^d/Γ and S^d/Γ' are isometric iff Γ and Γ' are conjugate in O(d+1). The volume of S^d/Γ equals vol(S^d)/|Γ|.

For each integer d ≥ 2, determine
   V(d) := sup { vol(S^d/Γ) : there exist finite subgroups Γ, Γ' ⊂ O(d+1) such that S^d/Γ and S^d/Γ' are Laplace-isospectral but not isometric },
or equivalently, determine the smallest possible order of Γ admitting such an isospectral non-isometric partner in dimension d.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is generally open. It has been conjectured that the largest-volume isospectral non-isometric pairs of spherical space forms are lens spaces, and this conjecture has been verified in dimensions n ≡ 2,3,4,5,6,7 (mod 9). Known constructions yield lower bounds such as vol(S^d)/8 (using almost-conjugate (Z/2Z)^3 subgroups) and vol(S^{2n-1})/11 in infinitely many odd dimensions, but the exact maximum is not known in general.

status_evidence.title: Isospectral spherical space forms and orbifolds of highest volume
status_evidence.snippet: It was conjectured that isospectral and non-isometric pairs of spherical space forms of highest volume are necessarily lens spaces; confirmed for n ≡ 2,3,4,5,6,7 mod 9.
status_evidence.claim: Highest-volume problem is partially resolved via a conjecture proven in certain residue classes of dimensions.
